title: The Invisibility of White Privilege with Brian Lowery, PhD

sentences.en: Over the past several weeks, protests against racial injustice have made headlines around the United States and the world.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几周里，抗议种族不公的示威活动成为了美国乃至全世界的头条新闻。

sentences.en: People of diverse backgrounds are turning out in large numbers in small towns and big
sentences.zh: 有着不同背景的人们纷纷涌上街头，无论是在小镇还是大

sentences.en: cities, incensed by recent high-profile instances where police have killed unarmed black people.
sentences.zh: 城市，他们都对最近备受关注的警察杀害无武装黑人事件感到愤怒。

sentences.en: For some white Americans, this movement may be prompting them to consider, some for the first time, the white privilege they've benefited from all their lives.
sentences.zh: 对于一些白人美国人来说，这场运动可能会促使他们思考他们一生中从中受益的白人特权，其中有些人甚至还是第一次思考。

sentences.en: What can psychologists' research tell us about how and why white Americans have long been able to ignore and even deny the advantages they enjoy merely for being white?
sentences.zh: 心理学研究能告诉我们关于白人美国人长期以来如何以及为什么能够忽视甚至否认他们仅仅因为是白人而享有的优势的哪些信息？

sentences.en: How do white people distance themselves from their privilege in order to preserve it?
sentences.zh: 白人如何为了维护自己的特权而与之保持距离？

sentences.en: And do they realize it when they do so?
sentences.zh: 当他们这样做时，他们意识到这一点了吗？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that explores the connections between psychological science and everyday lives.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学说话》，这是美国心理学协会的旗舰播客节目，探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Brian Lowry, a Senior Associate Dean and Professor of Organizational
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是布莱恩·劳瑞博士，他是斯坦福大学商学院的高级副院长兼组织

sentences.en: Behavior at Stanford University's Graduate School of Business.
sentences.zh: 行为学教授。

sentences.en: Dr. Lowry has studied the psychology of racial privilege in the U.S., including why white
sentences.zh: 劳瑞博士研究过美国的种族特权心理，包括为什么白人

sentences.en: Americans are often blind to their privilege and how they react when it's brought to their attention.
sentences.zh: 美国人往往对自己的特权视而不见，以及当这些特权被提出来时他们的反应。

sentences.en: Recently, he published an op-ed in the Washington Post describing his own experiences of racial
sentences.zh: 最近，他在《华盛顿邮报》上发表了一篇专栏文章，描述了他自己经历的种族

sentences.en: discrimination and calling on white Americans to support policies that advance racial justice.
sentences.zh: 歧视，并呼吁白人美国人支持促进种族公正的政策。

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, Dr. Lowry.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到《心理学说话》，劳瑞博士。

sentences.en: Hi, Kim.
sentences.zh: 嗨，金。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: In your op-ed, you discuss the racism you've experienced, including being targeted with racial slurs as a child and being unjustly stopped and searched by police as a teen.
sentences.zh: 在你的专栏文章中，你讨论了你所经历的种族主义，包括在童年时期成为种族侮辱的目标，以及在青少年时期遭到警察的不公正拦截和搜查。

sentences.en: You connect those experiences with your research on racial privilege.
sentences.zh: 你将这些经历与你关于种族特权的研究联系起来。

sentences.en: Why did you feel it was important to write this op-ed now and have this conversation?
sentences.zh: 为什么你觉得现在有必要写这篇专栏文章并进行这次对话？

sentences.en: That's a great question, Kim.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题，金。

sentences.en: I wanted people to realize that this is just how common it is.
sentences.zh: 我想让人们意识到这种情况是多么普遍。

sentences.en: And I think the recent videos and people's ability to see what's happening real time has increased that awareness.
sentences.zh: 我认为最近的视频以及人们实时看到正在发生的事情的能力提高了这种意识。

sentences.en: But I don't know that people have understood until recently just how common these kind of experiences are.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道人们直到最近才真正理解这类经历有多么普遍。

sentences.en: And I wanted to turn the focus from what's happening to black people in this country to what that means about the experience of white people in this country.
sentences.zh: 我想把焦点从这个国家的黑人身上发生的事情转移到这对这个国家的白人的经历意味着什么。

sentences.en: And so that's really what I thought was important to write it at this time.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是我认为在这个时候写这篇文章很重要的原因。

sentences.en: Much of your research has been on how white people make sense of the unfair advantages that our society confers on them.
sentences.zh: 你的许多研究都集中在白人如何理解社会赋予他们的不公优势。

sentences.en: In one paper, you talked about the three Ds, deny, distance, and dismantle, strategies that white people use to cope when confronted with evidence of white privilege.
sentences.zh: 在的一篇论文中，你谈到了“三个D”：否认、保持距离和瓦解，这是白人在面对白人特权的证据时用来应对的策略。

sentences.en: Can you talk a little bit more about those three Ds and the psychology behind each of those behaviors?
sentences.zh: 你能多谈谈这三个D以及每种行为背后的心理吗？

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So the first thing is that I think the psychology that drives it is a desire to feel like a good moral person.
sentences.zh: 所以第一点是，我认为推动这一现象的心理是成为一个好且有道德的人的渴望。

sentences.en: And in the context of a society that explains our outcomes as a function of deservingness, of meritocracy, it challenges our sense of self to believe that we might have benefited
sentences.zh: 在这样一个将我们的结果解释为应得性和精英统治功能的社会背景下，相信我们可能受益于

sentences.en: from unearned advantages.
sentences.zh: 未劳而获的优势会挑战我们的自我感。

sentences.en: And in the case of race, the idea that being white has conferred unfair unearned advantages can be incredibly uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 而在种族问题上，身为白人带来了不公且未劳而获的优势这一想法可能会让人感到无比的不舒服。

sentences.en: So I think that's the psychology that drives what we talk about in the deny, distance, and dismantle.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这就是驱动我们所讨论的否认、保持距离和瓦解背后的心理。

sentences.en: And so what actually happens, how that's managed, it can vary.
sentences.zh: 那么实际发生了什么，这是如何处理的，可能会有所不同。

sentences.en: One thing that white people do is to deny that they personally benefit from white advantage or white privilege.
sentences.zh: 白人做的一件事就是否认他们个人受益于白人优势或白人特权。

sentences.en: And this is done in multiple ways.
sentences.zh: 这是通过多种方式完成的。

sentences.en: One common way is to highlight hardships they face.
sentences.zh: 一个常见的方法是强调他们面临的困难。

sentences.en: And while we think those hardships are legitimate, that everyone faces legitimate, serious
sentences.zh: 虽然我们认为这些困难是合法的，每个人都面临着合法、严重的

sentences.en: hardships, hardships don't somehow absolve people of privileges or negate the existence of privileges.
sentences.zh: 困难，但困难并不能以某种方式免除人们的特权或否定特权的存在。

sentences.en: So that denial is an interesting strategy because as if you've gone through something hard in your life, that being white therefore doesn't confer advantages or privileges.
sentences.zh: 所以这种否认是一个有趣的策略，因为就好像如果你在生活中经历过艰难的事情，身为白人因此就不会赋予优势或特权。

sentences.en: Or it's the idea that privileges or advantages means that life is always easy for you, where that's not at all the case, and that's not the claim that we make.
sentences.zh: 或者这是一种认为特权或优势意味着生活对你来说总是轻而易举的想法，事实根本并非如此，也不是我们所声称的。

sentences.en: So that's the denial side.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是否认的一面。

sentences.en: And the distance one is interesting because the distance allows for the existence of privilege, but simply says that I don't benefit from it.
sentences.zh: 而保持距离的那一面很有趣，因为保持距离承认了特权的存在，但只是说我没有从中受益。

sentences.en: So it doesn't deny that privilege exists.
sentences.zh: 所以它并不否认特权的存在。

sentences.en: It doesn't deny that it could exist for other people, but you really kind of separate yourself
sentences.zh: 它并不否认它可能对其他人存在，但你确实把自己和

sentences.en: from other white people and say, I don't personally benefit, where denial is a way of sometimes denying the full existence of privilege.
sentences.zh: 其他白人区分开来，说我没有个人受益，而否认有时是否认特权完全存在的一种方式。

sentences.en: Meaning that nobody has white privilege.
sentences.zh: 意思是没有任何人拥有白人特权。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the example I gave was really personal, but you also see this, the denial in the way where
sentences.zh: 所以我给出的例子非常个人化，但你也可以看到这一点，通过

sentences.en: you see some people focusing on very successful black people, right, as a way of saying, look, they made it, therefore there isn't racial inequality.
sentences.zh: 看到一些人关注非常成功的黑人的方式来否认，对吧，以此来表明，看，他们成功了，因此不存在种族不平等。

sentences.en: Um, so there are other ways to get at that denial of privilege that it doesn't exist at all.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以还有其他方法来应对这种对特权根本不存在的否认。

sentences.en: And actually in this country, and so I think very recently, um, whites were claiming that they were, uh, at least a greater target of discrimination as black Americans are.
sentences.zh: 实际上在这个国家，所以我认为最近，嗯，白人们声称他们是，呃，至少是与美国黑人一样大的歧视目标。

sentences.en: Um, so there's, um, a lot of evidence that whites are uncomfortable with the possibility that white privilege exists at all.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以有很多证据表明，白人对白人特权可能根本存在的可能性感到不舒服。

sentences.en: And then, um, further that they personally benefit from it.
sentences.zh: 然后，嗯，更进一步，他们个人从中受益。

sentences.en: You've done research on how the way that you frame a discussion of racial inequality and privilege affects people's reactions to them.
sentences.zh: 你做过关于你如何构建对种族不平等和特权的讨论如何影响人们对它们的反应的研究。

sentences.en: Are there strategies to talk about racial privilege in a way that leads people to have a dismantle reaction rather than a denial or a distancing reaction?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么策略来讨论种族特权，从而引导人们产生瓦解的反应，而不是否认或保持距离的反应？

sentences.en: It's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: Um, when people are willing to accept that privilege exists, there's reason to believe that they might actually support policies that, um, dismantle it or work against it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当人们愿意接受特权的存在时，有理由相信他们实际上可能会支持那些，嗯，瓦解它或反对它的政策。

sentences.en: And it looks like when they don't, when people feel, um, more affirmed in their self, when they feel better about themselves, it's easier to acknowledge the existence of privilege.
sentences.zh: 看起来当他们不这样做时，当人们感到，嗯，自我得到更多肯定，当他们对自己的感觉更好时，就更容易承认特权的存在。

sentences.en: So that's what we do in a number of our papers.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们在多篇论文中所做的。

sentences.en: We, we show that when you affirm people's sense of self, when you give them the opportunity
sentences.zh: 我们，我们展示了当你肯定人们的自我感，当你给他们机会

sentences.en: to talk about what they value, what's important to them, that they're, um, they have an easier
sentences.zh: 谈论他们所珍视的东西、对他们重要的是什么时，他们，嗯，会更容易

sentences.en: time acknowledging the possibility that privilege exists and that they might benefit from it.
sentences.zh: 承认特权可能存在以及他们可能从中受益的可能性。

sentences.en: Um, and once people acknowledge the existence of privilege, if you can get people to see that it exists, then there's a, uh, greater likelihood and a, um, more, I wouldn't say
sentences.zh: 嗯，一旦人们承认了特权的存在，如果你能让人们看到它的存在，那么就会有，呃，更大的可能性和，呃，更强的，我不会说是

sentences.en: comfort, but a greater willingness to support policies that dismantle that privilege.
sentences.zh: 舒服，但更强烈的意愿去支持瓦解该特权的政策。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk for a moment about the invisibility of white privilege.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们花点时间讨论一下白人特权的隐蔽性。

sentences.en: In a recent research article, you wrote that white people in the United States often don't
sentences.zh: 在最近的一篇研究文章中，你写道美国的白人通常

sentences.en: even need to resort to the denial and distancing strategies we've talked about because of something you call herd invisibility.
sentences.zh: 甚至不需要诉诸我们所讨论的否认和保持距离策略，因为有一种你称之为群体隐蔽性的现象。

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思？

sentences.en: And how does herd invisibility happen?
sentences.zh: 群体隐蔽性是如何发生的？

sentences.en: I think it happens in part because the society is, is structured in a way to hide, um, the privilege that people benefit from.
sentences.zh: 我认为它的发生部分是因为社会的结构方式旨在隐藏，嗯，人们从中受益的特权。

sentences.en: So you can see this in obvious ways, for example, segregation, um, very few white folks in America
sentences.zh: 所以你可以在明显的方式中看到这一点，例如，隔离，嗯，美国的极少数白人

sentences.en: actually have black friends, um, and many fewer are, um, live in circumstances where they see the disadvantages or the racial inequity in our system.
sentences.zh: 实际上有黑人朋友，嗯，更少的人，嗯，生活在能够看到我们系统中的劣势或种族不平等的环境中。

sentences.en: So that, that segregation allows for people to be, remain blind to their own advantages because they don't see the disadvantages that exiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，这种隔离让人们能够对自己的优势视而不见，因为他们看不到存在的劣势。

sentences.en: So they don't see the racial inequities.
sentences.zh: 所以他们看不到种族不平等。

sentences.en: Um, they blind themselves to the racial inequities simply by the way, um, they go about their daily lives, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们仅仅通过他们，嗯，日常生活的方式，对种族不平等视而不见，对吧？

sentences.en: They don't have to make a conscious choice to, to ignore it so much as it's, um, hidden, it's hidden from them by the way that society is set up.
sentences.zh: 他们不必做出有意识的选择去，去忽略它，而是它被，它被社会的建立方式向他们隐藏了。

sentences.en: So that's one way that you get, um, herd invisibility.
sentences.zh: 所以这是产生，嗯，群体隐蔽性的其中一种方式。

sentences.en: And then each individual act, um, that, um, white people engage in to deny or distance actually
sentences.zh: 然后白人参与的每一个，嗯，用于否认或保持距离的个人行为，实际上

sentences.en: serves, um, the broader white community in that if I deny it exists and I create a narrative
sentences.zh: 都在为更广泛的白人社区服务，如果我否认它的存在，并且我创造了一个

sentences.en: that it doesn't exist, then that serves you, even if you aren't actively denying it yourself.
sentences.zh: 它不存在的叙事，那么这就会为你服务，即使你自己没有积极地否认它。

sentences.en: And these are some of the cloaking strategies that you described that people use to address some of the discomfort that they feel.
sentences.zh: 这些就是你所描述的人们用来解决他们感受到的某些不适的掩饰策略。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So again, going back to the underlying psychology, I think there's, when I talk about, we talk
sentences.zh: 所以再次回到潜在的心理，我认为，当我谈到，我们谈论

sentences.en: about invisibility, it's a interesting and ironic way to talk about it because in reality,
sentences.zh: 隐蔽性时，这是一种有趣且具有讽刺意味的说法，因为在现实中，

sentences.en: it, you have to be willfully ignorant not to see racial inequalities in our, in our society.
sentences.zh: 你必须刻意无知才能在我们社会的，我们的社会中看不到种族不平等。

sentences.en: Um, so the cloaking is a way of suggesting that what's happening is willful, but it doesn't require each individual person to participate at all times, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以掩饰是一种暗示正在发生的事情是刻意的方式，但它不需要每个人在所有时间都参与，对吧？

sentences.en: So that's the, the herd immunity part of the herd invisibility part.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是群体免疫的那部分，群体隐蔽性的部分。

sentences.en: Rather, if enough people engage in it, then it hides it.
sentences.zh: 相反，如果有足够多的人参与其中，它就会将其隐藏起来。

sentences.en: It allows, it allows an act of hiding from everyone, but it really is, this is what's I think often hard to convey that it really is an act of hiding.
sentences.zh: 它允许，它允许一种对所有人的隐藏行为，但它确实是，我认为这通常很难传达，即它确实是一种隐藏行为。

sentences.en: It's not, it's not, it's not that it can't be seen because the water we swim in, and that's sometimes how it's talked about.
sentences.zh: 它不是，它不是，它不是说看不见，因为我们游弋其中，有时人们就是这样谈论它的。

sentences.en: From my perspective, it's the disparities are so great, um, so stark and so easily, um, accessible
sentences.zh: 从我的角度来看，这种差距太大了，嗯，太明显了，而且太容易，嗯，接触到了，

sentences.en: that there really has to be some process in place to put, um, to allow us to not see
sentences.zh: 以至于必须有一些机制来置入，嗯，让我们看不到

sentences.en: it, that we have to engage in some psychological gymnastics, um, as a society to deny its existence.
sentences.zh: 它，作为一个社会，我们必须进行一些心理体操，嗯，来否认它的存在。

sentences.en: Um, and I think that's probably, um, well, not probably for white people, it's, there's discomfort when that, when they're not allowed to do that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这可能，嗯，对白人来说不是可能，当他们不被允许这样做时，会有不适感。

sentences.en: And for black people and other people of color, it's, um, it can be enraging to see people engage in this, these mental gymnastics in a way that allows them to ignore the
sentences.zh: 而对于黑人和其他有色人种来说，嗯，看到人们以一种允许他们忽视

sentences.en: pain of say the black community or, um, other communities of color.
sentences.zh: 比方说黑人社区或其他有色人种社区痛苦的方式进行这些心理体操，可能会令人怒不可遏。

sentences.en: Is the fact that so many white people are joining the protests evidence that at least some white
sentences.zh: 如此多的白人加入抗议活动，是否证明至少有一些白人

sentences.en: Americans are engaged in dismantling, even if they don't know that's what they're doing?
sentences.zh: 美国人正在参与瓦解，即使他们不知道这就是他们正在做的事情？

sentences.en: I certainly hope so.
sentences.zh: 我当然希望如此。

sentences.en: Um, I should just say that I don't, I don't personally tend toward optimism.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我应该说我个人并不倾向于乐观。

sentences.en: Um, and some of that I think is, is realism.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为其中一些是现实主义。

sentences.en: Like I, I, I, the history of the United States is, um, littered with movements that in the moment
sentences.zh: 就像我，我，美国的历史，嗯，充斥着这样的运动，在当时

sentences.en: seemed, um, uh, seemed like they were gaining traction, but there's, uh, inevitably been a backlash to those movements.
sentences.zh: 看起来，嗯，呃，似乎正在获得关注，但对这些运动的强烈反弹是不可避免的。

sentences.en: Um, and that backlash tends to come when, when you move beyond simple, the, simply the sense
sentences.zh: 嗯，这种反弹往往发生在你超越了简单的，人们从指出其他人经历的痛苦中获得的道德利益感，

sentences.en: of moral benefit that people have from pointing out the pain that other people experience to the necessary work of actually changing the system, which comes at a personal coSt.
sentences.zh: 转向实际改变系统的必要工作时，而这伴随着个人代价。

sentences.en: So the question will be when it comes at a personal cost, will the energy that we see now in the streets remain?
sentences.zh: 所以问题在于，当它伴随着个人代价时，我们在街头看到的能量还会持续吗？

sentences.en: And those personal costs mean giving up some of the privilege, right?
sentences.zh: 而这些个人代价意味着放弃一些特权，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, you have to share some of the pie.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你必须分享一部分蛋糕。

sentences.en: Yes, that I think that, um, I think it may be hard for white people to fully understand the benefits of being white in the society.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为，嗯，我认为白人可能很难完全理解在这个社会中身为白人的好处。
